data: Status: planned (wave 3). No code exists. The package name is provisional, and so is the home: the bibliography leaves open whether the solver lives here or in go-numerics/integrate, which has stiff ODE solvers (Radau, BDF) and event handling but no DAE support and no mass matrix.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion DAE error against the reference solution of the Bari test set at a stated tolerance; index-1 constraint residual; final-time error, constraint drift, steps, Newton iterations; event times to 1e-10 Reference implementations: SUNDIALS (IDA, BSD-3-Clause), DASSL from netlib (SLATEC, public domain) and Hairer’s RADAU5 (BSD-2-style licence). The Bari Test Set for IVP Solvers is the corpus; its licence is unspecified, so the cases are generated and cited, never redistributed. Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference.

data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: Index-1 systems in fully implicit form, F(t, y, y’) = 0, by a variable-order, variable-step BDF method (DASSL and IDA). Semi-explicit systems M y’ = f and mass-matrix problems, through Radau IIA. Consistent initial conditions. Events: zero crossings and discontinuities, restarting on dense output. Without an expression system, only index-1 systems and user-supplied reduced systems are feasible; index reduction belongs to model.

data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion Riccati and Lyapunov relative residual below 1e3·n·eps, a solution symmetric to one ulp, closed-loop poles in the left half-plane; the worst residual over the benchmark set and the median ratio against SLICOT and SciPy are reported c2d relative error against a high-precision reference, 10·eps norm-wise Reference implementations: SLICOT-Reference (BSD-3-Clause in the repository; each routine’s header is to be checked, and the commit recorded, before any port), SciPy (solve_continuous_are, place_poles), python-control and Octave’s control package as oracles. The SLICOT benchmark collections and COMPleib are the corpora. Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference.

data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: Continuous and discrete algebraic Riccati equations (CARE, DARE). Lyapunov and Sylvester equations. LQR, LQG and Kalman gains. Pole placement for multi-input systems. Discretisation (c2d): zero-order hold, first-order hold, Tustin and matched. It depends on lti and on Schur reordering, QZ and expm in go-ndarray’s linalg.

data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion poles and zeros relative error against the reference after sorting, with the conditioning accounted for frequency response complex relative error per point against python-control, reported in ULPs of the response expm relative error against a high-precision reference, norm-wise time response agreement with the expm-based exact solution; an ODE-based path is judged with a tolerance Reference implementations: python-control (BSD-3-Clause; the API template), SciPy’s scipy.signal, and Octave’s control package as an oracle only, since it is GPL. Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference, no slower than it on one core.

Appl. 31(3), 2009, doi:10.1137/09074721X stability margins Skogestad and Postlethwaite, Multivariable Feedback Control, 2nd ed., Wiley 2005 textbook examples Franklin, Powell and Emami-Naeini, Feedback Control of Dynamic Systems, 8th ed., Pearson 2019
data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: Model types: transfer function, zero-pole-gain, state space and frequency-response data. Model algebra: series, parallel and feedback connections. Poles, zeros, DC gain and minimal realisation. Time response (step, impulse, arbitrary input, initial condition), exact for LTI models through the matrix exponential. Frequency response, Nyquist encirclements, root locus and stability margins. It needs the non-symmetric eigenvalue solver, QZ and expm that go-ndarray’s linalg does not yet provide.

data: Status: planned (wave 4, item 22 of the plan). No code exists. The package name is provisional. It comes after the DAE solver and go-symbolic, the size is XL, and the roadmap states plainly that MapleSim parity is a product, not a library: MapleSim’s component libraries are proprietary and are not planned.
data.how-it-will-be-validated#How it will be: Area Criterion DAE and modelling detected index, constraint drift and final-time error against Modelica reference runs The corpus is the Modelica Standard Library examples (BSD-3-Clause). OpenModelica (OSMC-PL and GPL-3) is an oracle only and is never ported; Maple is proprietary and is never run as an oracle. Every item also needs unit tests at 100% coverage and a performance table against the reference.

data.what-it-will-provide#What it will provid: Connectors and equation assembly. Index reduction by Pantelides’ algorithm and the dummy-derivative method, on go-symbolic equations. Structural analysis and block-lower-triangular ordering (Tarjan’s strongly connected components), which also finds algebraic loops. Emission of Go through go-symbolic’s codegen. A Modelica-subset reader, last. Full Modelica compatibility is out of reach and will be said so in the README.
